corpus_gaps: Stamp duty rates for a transfer of immovable property are fixed by Ministerial Order under the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, s.3; no such Order is in the corpus, so the answer says duty must be provided for without quantifying it.
Notarial fees are governed by rules under the Notaries Ordinance, s.40; the fee scale itself is not in the corpus.

The conveyancing conventions of tracing title for thirty years and of calling for a non-vesting certificate, street line and building line certificate and up-to-date rates and tax receipts are professional practice rather than statute; no provision in the corpus prescribes them, so they are not asserted as statutory steps.

The corpus records amendment years only, not commencement dates. The Notaries (Amendment) Act, No. 6 of 2024 and the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act, No. 4 of 2024 both carry the year 2024 and it cannot be established from the corpus whether they were in force in April 2024. No indispensable provision here depends on a 2024 change.

The Agrarian Development Act and coconut-specific fragmentation or development legislation are not in the corpus, so any restriction they might place on the sale of a coconut plantation could not be checked.

Local authority requirements for the bungalow fall under the Pradeshiya Sabhas Act, which is not in the corpus; only the Municipal Councils and Urban Councils Ordinances are, and neither applies to a rural Kurunegala estate.

The corpus body of Notaries Ordinance section 31 runs the rules together and does not print the numbers of rules (7A), (15A), (16) and (17); those labels in this map are reconstructed from the order and content of the paragraphs, so a lawyer should confirm the rule numbers against a printed edition before the map is used for citation.

provisions.why_relevant: Imposes the notary's core pre-drafting duty on a purchase: search the land registry to establish the state of the vendor's title and prior registered dealings.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: Each step a notary must take on a purchase of land is prescribed by statute: the requirement of notarial writing and attestation, the pre-drafting registry search and certified folio extract, the description of the land, the true consideration, stamp duty, identification of executants, the contents of the attestation and the thirty-day registration deadline. The consequence of failing to search or register is supplied by the registration statute, and the ceiling and consent regimes that could bite on a thirty-acre plantation are also statutory. A practitioner would in addition follow conveyancing conventions such as tracing title for thirty years, but every step in the gold answer is tied to a provision recorded here, so no judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is indispensable.

legal_issues.issue: What the notary must do before drawing the deed: verify his own competence for the area, call for the vendor's title deeds and search the land registry for the state of the title and registered encumbrances.
How the disclosed mortgage over the estate must be dealt with, and how the purchaser's priority is protected between search and registration.
What the deed itself must contain: an accurate description of the thirty-acre estate and bungalow by boundaries, extent and administrative situation, and the true and full consideration.
Whether any statutory ceiling or consent regime applies to the purchase of a thirty-acre coconut estate.
What the notary must do at and after execution: identification, witnesses, attestation, stamp duty and registration within the statutory period.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps across enactments: (1) the transaction must be by notarially attested deed; (2) that duty carries with it the notary's own pre-drafting search and certified folio extract, the description and consideration requirements and the attestation rules; and (3) the point of the search and of the thirty-day registration deadline is supplied by a different enactment, under which an unregistered instrument is void against a later registered one. Only indispensable dependencies are counted. Verified: the six provisions added by the verifier (the search proviso, the two-witness and reading-over rules, the priority-notice relation-back, the transferee's signature and the post-commencement ceiling vesting) sit inside the three enactments already counted and add no further hop.

He is a citizen of Sri Lanka, resident in Colombo 5, and he owns no other agricultural land. The property is known as Pinnaduwa Watta, depicted as Lot 1 in Survey Plan No. 4127 dated 12 June 2019 made by K. You are authorised to practise in Sinhala in the Kurunegala district and your office is at Kurunegala.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What steps the notary retained by the intending purchaser of a thirty-acre coconut estate with a bungalow in Kurunegala must take before, at and after the execution of the conveyance.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A sale of land is of no force in law unless the deed is in writing and signed by every executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary who attests it (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a)). A notary may act only in the area and language for which he is authorised (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule 22). Before drawing a deed affecting an interest in land he must search the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title and whether any prior deed has been registered (s.31 rule 17(a)) and must obtain from the Registrar the certified extract of the folio showing ownership and registered encumbrances (s.31 rule 17(b)(i)); the registry books may be searched and certified extracts obtained by a person interested or his agent (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.42). The search matters because an unregistered instrument is void against a party claiming adversely for value under a later duly registered instrument (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7(1)), and a transferee for value may lodge a priority notice which holds for six weeks and back-dates registration (s.30(5)). On a transfer the notary must use his best endeavours to obtain the vendor's title deed and endorse the new deed's particulars on it (s.31 rule 33). The deed must carry an accurate description of the land by boundaries, extent and situation with the district, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and Grama Niladhari Division (s.31 rule 16(a)), and the true and full consideration must be ascertained and set out (Notaries Ordinance s.38(1)). The notary may not attest without an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided (s.31 rule 6), duty being payable by him (s.31 rule 7A(a)) and charged on every specified instrument (Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act s.3(1)). He must identify the executants from personal knowledge or their identity documents (s.31 rule 9), attest without delay under his signature and seal recording execution, identification, date, place, reading over, consideration paid in his presence and stamps (s.31 rule 20), and submit the deed for registration within thirty days of attestation (s.31 rule 30A). Two statutory restrictions must be excluded: agricultural land other than paddy may not be owned above fifty acres (Land Reform Law s.3(1)(b)), and land held on a state grant cannot be disposed of without the prior approval of the Government Agent (Land Development Ordinance s.19(6)); a consent certificate of the Board is required only for tea or rubber estates (Tea and Rubber Estates (Control of Fragmentation) Act s.3(1)).
gold_answer_draft.application: The estate lies at Wariyapola in the Kurunegala District and the notary is authorised to practise in Sinhala in that district, so he may accept the retainer and attest the deed. He should take full instructions, call for and examine the vendor's prior deeds, beginning with Deed of Transfer No. 1032 of 1998 and tracing back through the 1979 partition decree, and search the Kurunegala land registry folio in which that deed is registered, taking a certified folio extract. That extract should disclose Bond No. 2210 of 2021 in favour of the bank, and the notary must arrange for a registered discharge, or for the bank's release to be executed and registered simultaneously with the conveyance out of the purchase money; otherwise the client would take subject to that earlier registered interest. Because execution is not to take place until 20 May 2024, a priority notice should be considered so that no instrument executed by the vendor in the interval gains priority. The thirty-acre extent and the boundaries of Lot 1 in Survey Plan No. 4127 must be checked on the ground against the folio description and reproduced in the schedule with the village, Divisional Secretary's Division and district, the bungalow being described with the land. The whole thirty acres is coconut and the client owns no other agricultural land, so the purchase leaves him below the fifty-acre ceiling; coconut is neither tea nor rubber, so no consent certificate is needed; and as the chain shows private freehold with no state permit or grant, no approval of the Government Agent is called for. The full price of Rs. 42,000,000, including the Rs. 4,200,000 advance paid under the agreement of 10 January 2024, must be set out as the consideration, and the balance paid at execution recorded in the attestation with the details of any cheque or draft. Stamp duty on that value must be provided for and paid before attestation. At execution the notary must identify both parties from their national identity cards, have two witnesses of good repute sign, read over and explain the deed, then attest, sign and seal it without delay, endorse the particulars on the vendor's title deed, and lodge the deed for registration by 19 June 2024.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The notary's steps are, in sequence: confirm his competence for the area and take instructions; call for and examine the vendor's title deeds; search the Kurunegala land registry and obtain a certified folio extract; deal with the disclosed mortgage and consider a priority notice; verify extent and boundaries against the survey plan; satisfy himself that no ceiling or consent regime bars the purchase; draw the deed with an accurate schedule and the true and full consideration; provide for and pay stamp duty; execute and attest the deed with identified parties and two witnesses; and submit it for registration within thirty days of attestation. On these facts nothing in the statutory material bars the purchase, provided the bond is discharged and the deed is properly drawn, attested and registered in time.

answer_claims.claim_text: A sale of land has no force in law unless the deed is in writing, signed by every executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary who attests it, so the transaction has to be carried through by a notary.
A notary may only attest a deed in the area and language in which he is authorised to practise.

Before drawing any deed affecting an interest in land the notary must search, or cause to be searched, the registers in the land registry to ascertain the state of the title and whether any prior deed affecting the land has been registered.

The notary must obtain from the Registrar of the relevant Land Registry a certified extract of the folio containing the last entry showing the ownership of and the registered encumbrances on the land.
The registry duplicates, books and indexes may be searched by a person interested or by his agent duly authorised in writing, and certified extracts obtained.

An instrument that is not duly registered is void against a party claiming an adverse interest for valuable consideration under a later instrument that is duly registered, so priority depends on registration.

A person acquiring an interest in land for valuable consideration may lodge a priority notice, which remains in force for six weeks and back-dates the registration of the instrument to the date of the notice.
The notary must use his best endeavours to obtain the vendor's title deed on a transfer and endorse on it the number and date of the new deed and the nature of the transaction.

The deed must embody, in itself or in an annexed schedule, an accurate and clear description of the land showing its boundaries, extent and situation, specifying the district, Divisional Secretary's Division, local authority division and Grama Niladhari Division.
The notary must endeavour to ascertain the true and full consideration and set it out in the deed.

The notary may not attest unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided, and stamp duty on the instrument is payable by the notary, duty being charged on every specified instrument at the rate the Minister determines.
The notary must establish the identity of the executants, either by personal knowledge or by inspecting the national identity card, passport bio-page or driving licence.

The notary must without delay attest the deed and sign and seal an attestation recording, among other things, execution in his presence and in the presence of one another, how the executants were identified, the date and place, the reading over, the consideration actually paid in his presence and the stamps.
The attested deed must be submitted for registration within thirty days of attestation.
A person may not own more than fifty acres of agricultural land where the land is not exclusively paddy, and land owned in excess of that ceiling vests in the Commission.
Land alienated on a state grant may not be disposed of except with the prior approval of the Government Agent, and not in portions below the minimum specified in the grant.
Prior consent of the Board, evidenced by a certificate attached to the deed, is required only for the transfer of a tea or rubber estate.

The notary should also satisfy himself that an out-and-out purchase is the transaction the parties actually intend and explain the deed to them before signature, although this express duty was introduced by an amendment of 2024 whose commencement relative to April 2024 is not established on the corpus.
Because the estate lies at Wariyapola in the Kurunegala District and the notary is authorised to practise in Sinhala in that district, he may accept the retainer and attest the deed himself.

The vendor's assertion that he owns on Deed of Transfer No. 1032 of 1998, traced back to the 1979 partition decree, must be tested by searching the Kurunegala land registry folio in which that deed is registered and by obtaining the certified folio extract, and the notary should call for and examine the prior deeds themselves.

The search and folio extract should disclose Bond No. 2210 of 2021 in favour of the bank, so the notary must arrange for a registered discharge or for the release to be executed and registered together with the conveyance, since otherwise the buyer takes subject to that earlier registered interest.

Because the bond is outstanding and execution is not to take place until 20 May 2024, the notary should consider lodging a priority notice so that an instrument executed by the vendor in the interval cannot gain priority over the client's conveyance.

The schedule to the deed must reproduce the thirty-acre extent and the boundaries of Lot 1 in Survey Plan No. 4127 with the village, Divisional Secretary's Division and district, and the notary should have the plan checked on the ground against the folio description before drawing the deed.

Since the whole thirty acres is coconut land and the client owns no other agricultural land, the purchase leaves his holding well below the fifty-acre ceiling, but the notary should record that check.
Coconut is neither tea nor rubber, so no consent certificate of the Board needs to be obtained or attached to this deed.
The chain shows private freehold and no state permit or grant, so no prior approval of the Government Agent has to be obtained before the vendor conveys.

The full price of Rs. 42,000,000, including the Rs. 4,200,000 advance already paid under the agreement of 10 January 2024, must be set out in the deed as the consideration, and the balance paid at execution must be recorded in the attestation with the details of any cheque or bank draft.
Stamp duty on that consideration must be worked out, provided for and paid by the notary before he attests, and the receipt or stamps dealt with as the rules require.

At execution the notary must identify Mr. Ranasinghe and the vendor from their national identity cards, have two witnesses of good repute sign, read over and explain the deed, and then attest, sign and seal it without delay.

If the deed is executed on 20 May 2024 it must be lodged for registration in the Kurunegala land registry by 19 June 2024, and the notary should also endorse the particulars of the new deed on the vendor's title deed.

The notary's steps therefore run in sequence: confirm his own competence for the area, call for and examine the vendor's title deeds, search the land registry and take a certified folio extract, deal with the disclosed mortgage and consider a priority notice, verify the extent and boundaries against the survey plan, check that no statutory ceiling or consent regime bites, draw the deed with an accurate schedule and the true consideration, provide for stamp duty, execute and attest it with identified parties and two witnesses, and lodge it for registration within thirty days.
On the enriched facts nothing in the frozen statutory material bars the purchase, provided the bank's bond is discharged and the deed is properly drawn, attested and registered in time.
